title: Roll: a ball on a board, in three dimensions, with physics and sound
brief: Build a small game called Roll. It is in three dimensions and has one board.
The game
- Lengths are in metres, y is up. The board is a flat square slab 6 wide (x from -3 to 3) and 6 deep (z from -3 to 3), 0.2 thick, with its top face at y = 0. It has no walls.

- A ball of radius 0.25 starts at rest with its centre at (0, 1.25, 0), one metre above the board. Gravity pulls it down at 9.81 m/s2. It lands on the board, bounces at least once (each bounce lower than the one before) and comes to rest on the board with its centre at y = 0.25. The ball is a rigid body: it rolls, it keeps moving when a push ends and slows only gently, and it falls when it leaves the board's edge.

- The player pushes the ball: Right (D) toward +x, Left (A) toward -x, Up (W) away from the camera toward -z, Down (S) toward the camera, +z. A push accelerates the ball by 4 m/s2 in that direction for as long as it is held, whether the ball is on the board or in the air.

- Four coins float 0.25 above the board at (2, 0.25, 0), (-2, 0.25, 0), (0, 0.25, 2) and (0, 0.25, -2). The ball takes a coin when its centre comes within 0.5 of the coin's: 10 points, the coin is gone, and the sound `coin` plays.
- A ball whose centre drops below y = -5 has fallen: one of 3 lives is lost, the sound `fall` plays, and the ball is put back at rest at its start, (0, 1.25, 0). The coins already taken stay taken.
- Each time the ball lands on the board at more than 1 m/s the sound `bounce` plays.

- The run is won when all four coins are taken, and lost when the third life is lost. After either, nothing moves and nothing scores until a restart (Enter), which begins a fresh run: 4 coins, 3 lives, score 0, the ball at its start.
- The screen shows the score and the lives left; after the end it shows "You win" or "Game over", the score and how to restart.
- The view is in perspective: a camera at (0, 6, 8) looking at (0, 0, 0), about 50 degrees of vertical field of view, with light and shade that show the ball is round and the board is a slab.
- The game advances in fixed steps of 1/60 second. What happens never depends on how fast frames are drawn, and the same inputs at the same ticks always give the same game.
- The three sounds (`coin`, `bounce`, `fall`) are the game's own, each under half a second, and each can be told from the other two by ear.
Checkable without hands
Someone who cannot play it by hand will check it, so the game must offer three things, however you build it:

1. A headless run: given a number of ticks and a script of inputs (at tick T: left, right, up, down, none or restart; an input holds until the next one), it runs that many ticks with no window and prints the state as one JSON object: {"tick" (the ticks run so far in this headless run), "score", "lives", "over", "won", "ball": {"x", "y", "z"} (its centre), "coins": [{"x", "z"}] (the coins not yet taken), "sounds": [..] (the name of every sound played so far in this run, in order)}.
2. A frame: after such a run, the view as it would be drawn, written as a PNG 640 pixels wide and 480 tall.
3. Each sound as a WAV file: either the files themselves in the work folder, or the exact command that writes one.
Hand in, in your work folder
- The game, ready to run.
- README.md: how to play it, the exact commands for the headless run, the frame and the sounds, and what you checked yourself and how.

acceptance.text: The headless run exists, takes a tick count and an input script, and prints the state as the brief's JSON object.
The frame is written as a 640 x 480 PNG after a headless run.
Each of the three sounds (coin, bounce, fall) can be had as a WAV file by what the README says; each is under half a second, not silent, and the three are not the same sound.

With no input the ball falls from y = 1.25, first reaches the board (y at or below 0.3) between tick 20 and tick 40, rises again after that (a bounce: its y goes back above 0.3), and after 600 ticks rests with y within 0.05 of 0.25 and x and z within 0.1 of 0.
`bounce` is in `sounds` by tick 60 of a run with no input, and it is not added again and again while the ball rests (no more than 6 in 600 ticks).
Holding right moves the ball toward +x, left toward -x, up toward -z and down toward +z; after a push ends on the board the ball keeps moving the same way for at least 30 more ticks.
A ball pushed right from rest reaches the coin at (2, 0): `score` becomes 10, that coin leaves `coins` (3 left), and `coin` is added to `sounds`; nothing else scores.

A ball pushed right without stopping leaves the board's edge and falls (its y goes below 0); when its y would pass -5, `lives` goes from 3 to 2, `fall` is added to `sounds`, and the ball is back near (0, 1.25, 0) falling from rest; coins taken stay taken.
After the third fall `over` is true and `won` false, `lives` is 0, and further ticks and inputs (other than restart) change neither the score, the lives, the ball nor the coins.
There is a script that takes all four coins without losing three lives; after the fourth `won` and `over` are true, `score` is 40 and `coins` is empty, and further ticks change nothing.
A restart after the end begins a fresh run: score 0, 3 lives, 4 coins, the ball at its start, `over` and `won` false.
Two headless runs with the same ticks and script print identical states.

The frame of a run in play is a view in perspective from above and in front: the board's far edge is drawn shorter than its near edge, the ball is drawn where the state puts it and is shaded as a round thing, the coins not yet taken are drawn at their places and a taken coin is not drawn.
The frame shows the score and the lives left; the frame after the end shows "You win" or "Game over", the score and how to restart.
README.md says how to play and gives commands for the three checks that work as written.
